svg.title: Original and standardised boundaries identify the same normal event
svg.desc: X has normal mean one hundred and variance two hundred twenty-five, so its standard deviation is fifteen. The density curve shades the original interval from eighty-five to one hundred thirty. A second horizontal scale labels the same boundaries by their standardised scores minus one and two. The probability is Phi of two minus Phi of minus one, approximately zero point eight one eight six using unrounded calculator probabilities. Using CDF entries rounded to four decimal places instead gives zero point nine seven seven two minus zero point one five eight seven, equal to zero point eight one eight five. This last-digit difference is table rounding, not a different event. The vertical axis is density, not point probability.
